first_touch.text: In a match of SMITE, across the five chaotic game modes and countless warriors, two players had no idea that destiny was loading beside them. You’re playing Surt, a fiery giant of chaos. The battle begins. On your team: a Merlin and an Artemis—unassuming gods, just like any other. But something about Artemis’s playstyle catches your attention. It’s graceful. Thoughtful. Human.

choices.text: Keep playing normally, but stay close to Artemis
Keep playing without interest

curious_connection.text: You don’t really care about your teammates. You’re here to win. But something… draws your attention. Not the objectives. Not the chaos of the battlefield. It’s her. The Artemis on your team. Precise. Unafraid. She doesn’t ping. She simply moves, and you start moving with her. Then, out of nowhere… a whisper pops up on your screen: 'Hey… can I send you a friend request?' You hesitate. Just a game, right?

choices.text: Accept the request and add her on Discord
Ignore it. You don’t mix games with people
Say: 'Only if you promise to carry me next game.'

begin_connection.text: You accept. Seconds later, a friend request on Discord. Her name pops up. You feel nervous but reply: 'Good job 👏👍' She responds immediately: 'You were fun to play with, also very kind.' One game becomes five. Then a week of nights spent online. Somehow, a tiny request became the beginning of everything.  You suggest a voice call. She’s shy, quiet, barely speaking but you hear her smile in the silence. Her English is soft but clear, and you make a quiet vow: you’ll never laugh at her voice, only listen harder

choices.text: Break the silence with a joke
Push her to talk more, even if she’s not ready
Say nothing, but stay

missed_chance.text: You say nothing. The match ends. You close the screen. You try to forget about it. But something lingers… The way you played together. The way she typed that message. What if?

choices.text: You finally message her, even if it's late
Queue up again, hoping to find her by chance
Let it go and never message her again

delayed_hope.text: You type slowly, carefully.  “Hey… I’m sorry I didn’t say anything that night. I wanted to.” You hit send. Minutes pass. Then: “It’s okay. I was nervous too.” Just like that, the door cracks open again. And this time, you’re not too late

choices.text: You ask for her discord and send her a friend request
You decide to ask her to play ranked joust next time

ranked_joust.text: She’s not just friendly, kind and dangerous in the right hands. Definitely duo material, she's the perfect mix of skill and heart. Exactly the kind of teammate you dream about. So you dare to ask if she wants to be your duo and she accepts. And just like that, a great duo in this game is born.

friends_discord.text: You started to talk to her, you sent your picture and she sent her picture back. She’s beautiful, you got into her that’s how you decide to talk to her everyday.

first_real_love.text: You started talking more, the words flowing easier now that the ice was broken. One night, almost without thinking, you sent her a picture of yourself. A pause. Then, her reply came a photo of her, smiling softly, like the moment had been waiting for both of you. She was beautiful. Not just in the obvious way, but in the kind of way that made you want to memorize her face, the curve of her smile, the light in her eyes. Something shifted in you. The game that brought you together suddenly felt like the smallest part of the story. From that day on, talking to her became your favorite part of every day, a constant, a comfort, a pull you didn’t want to fight. Somewhere between matches and midnight conversations, you knew: you didn’t just want to play the game with her. You wanted to be part of her world.

serendipity_retry.text: You log in. Same time. Same mode. Just in case. It feels silly. Maybe even desperate. But then… Familiar username. You freeze. She’s on your team. You ping an objective like old times. This time, she types: “You came back.”

choices.text: Happily you sent her a friend request cause coincidence is a sign.
You type: “Maybe this time we could call? Just for the game.” She then sends: “Sure why not?”

sign_coincidence.text: You send her a friend request without hesitation because moments like this don’t happen twice by accident. She accepts. Her Discord ID arrives in your inbox a moment later, like a tiny bridge between two worlds. The call starts simple. Light chatter about the match. The game fades into the background as you realize you’re listening more to her voice than to the sounds of battle. There’s something warm in the way she laughs unguarded, like you’ve known each other longer than you have. You start sharing little pieces of your world. She tells you about her day; you tell her about the sky where you are. The match ends, but neither of you clicks “leave call.” Minutes turn to hours, and it feels as if the night was made for finding her again.  You realize then: it wasn’t just a coincidence. It was a sign. And you’re not letting it pass this time

ask_for_call.text: She accepts your friend request and sends her Discord ID. The call starts with light, playful chitchat until you realize she’s been drinking. Maybe that’s why she’s more open tonight, her laughter bubbling through the mic. You like it. You lean into it, tossing jokes just to hear that sound again. The match ends, but you both stay in the call. She says she can’t play anymore “I’m too drunk,” she admits with a giggle. You close the game too. Now it’s just the two of you talking about everything and nothing. You step outside and start describing the donkeys you can see from where you’re standing. She laughs again, then complains about the fan in her room “It’s so loud,” she says. Then her voice shifts. Panic. She’s too drunk, and the world is spinning for her. You speak softly, telling her to breathe, to focus on your voice. You wish you could be there, right now, just to make sure she’s okay.

what_happened_yest.text: What started as a casual match turned into a night you’ll never forget. One playful request for a call, and suddenly her voice is in your ears warm, unguarded, and touched with a tipsy boldness that makes her laugh more freely than usual. You find yourself chasing that sound, throwing out jokes just to hear it again. The game ends, but the conversation doesn’t. From silly talk about donkeys outside your window to her teasing complaints about a noisy fan, the night feels oddly intimate. But when the laughter fades into panic, you stay. Calm words, steady tone, promising she’s safe. You wish you could cross the distance in an instant. That night leaves a mark one you’ll think about every time you remember how her voice sounded when she let her guard down.

choices.text: You open up
Make a promise

flirty_banter.text: You reply: 'Only if you promise to carry me next game too.' Artemis replies instantly: 'Deal. But only if you stop stealing all the kills' You both laugh. The mood is lighter now. You win. Barely. But it feels like more than just a victory. She asks for your Discord, and before long, you’re talking more about life than the game. And one night she says: 'I didn’t expect to meet someone like you here.'

choices.text: ‘If we win the next game, you have to send me a picture.’
‘You know, if we keep talking like this, I’m going to start thinking you’re flirting with me.’

suggestive_tease.text: She doesn’t reply right away, and for a second you wonder if you pushed too far. Then: “And what if I am?” Your fingers hover over the keyboard. The match continues, but you’re barely paying attention. “Then I guess I’ll have to flirt back.” Her next message is simple: “Good. I was hoping you’d say that.” From then on, every word between you feels charged.

not_as_spicy.text: The air between you changes thicker now, charged with something neither of you has to name. The game’s still going, but the real match is happening in the way your words dance around each other. Every line feels like it’s balancing on the edge of a dare.

choices.text: Double down
Go soft instead of spicy

playful_challenge.text: You stare at her picture longer than you should. It’s more than just a photo it’s a little piece of her world that she decided to share with you. There’s a confidence in her smile, a sparkle in her eyes that says she knows exactly what she’s doing. It’s your move now, and you realize… how you respond might change everything.

choices.text: Send your picture right away.
Send a hot picture

focus_connection.text: You shake your head and shift your focus back to the game. There's no time for distractions, not even the kind that makes your heart twitch unexpectedly. The team pulls through. Victory. Just another match in your history. You close the client, no friend requests accepted. No messages answered. Just silence—and for now, that feels safe.

choices.text: Start a romantic ‘what could’ve been’ journey
Do nothing

alterative_line.text: You never planned on finding anything unusual in West Virginia. It was just a trip. One quiet afternoon in a bar, you overhear a girl talking behind you: 'Yeah, I like Artemis in SMITE.' Your breath catches. You turn and ask, 'What’s your in-game name?' 'Pudin,' she says. It’s her.

choices.text: Walk over and say: 'Pudin? From SMITE? I can’t believe it’s actually you.'
Sit nearby and wait for the right moment to catch her eye

closed_ending.text: You never see her again. Maybe it was one of those once-in-a-lifetime matches. Maybe she deleted the game. Or changed her name. You tell yourself it didn’t matter. But sometimes, in the quiet moments, when you hear the SMITE menu music play… You wonder what would’ve happened if you'd just typed one word: 'Sure.'

break_silence.text: ‘You know... if someone accuses you of murder one day, the police will definitely arrest you. You’re way too quiet—they’ll just assume you’re guilty.’ Silence. Then a laugh. A real one. That laugh broke the tension like glass shattering. You didn’t even care that you lost the match.

choices.text: Message her the next day
Cause you didn’t like how she was doing you prefer to lead this to a beautiful friendship.
Sing a song

just_friends.text: From then on, things settled into an easy rhythm. We queued together almost every other night, picking gods we knew would complement each other. I’d dive in recklessly, she’d cover my back. Sometimes we won by a landslide, sometimes we got crushed so hard we couldn’t stop laughing. Outside of the matches, our Discord chats became a quiet corner of my day, links to funny reels, pictures of her pets, random “good luck” messages before games. She told me about her favorite snacks, I told her about my weird pre-game rituals. It never crossed the line into late-night confessions or anything heavy. And that was fine. Because some connections aren’t about fireworks they’re about showing up, game after game, knowing someone’s there. Months later, I’d scroll through my friend list and see her name light up. No matter how the day had gone, I’d smile. She was my duo, my co-op partner, my constant in a lobby full of strangers. Not every story is a love story. But this one, in its own way, was perfect.

straight_communication.text: Passing the days, you realize something about her is desirable. You find out she’s from Mexico, and you’re from Georgia. You type: 'It’s not really thatttt far. Just a couple of miles, kilometers.The games keep coming, but now every match feels different. It’s not just about winning, it’s about playing with her. Between rounds, you learn little pieces of her life: her favorite snacks, the way she laughs when she’s caught off guard, how I call her “my pudin”. Then comes the detail that makes you pause she’s in Mexico. You’re in Georgia. A border, a thousand miles, a map full of distance but it feels like she’s closer than anyone.

choices.text: Wait for her to suggest meeting
Tell her you’ll travel to Mexico

sing_song.text: You know she’s nervous and shy, but you take the lead, hoping humor will make her comfortable. Deep down, you’re dying to hear her voice.

being_humoristic.text: You know she’s nervous and shy, but you decide to take the lead in the conversation, hoping that being a little funnier might make her feel comfortable enough to speak. Deep down, you’re dying to hear her voice not just the occasional giggle, but words, sentences, her rhythm. So you throw out little jokes, testing the waters. Some fall flat, met with that shy silence that makes you wonder if she’s smiling or hiding. Others earn you a soft laugh, the kind that hits your chest like a spark. And in those moments, the quiet doesn’t feel heavy anymore it feels like a game you both know how to play. The match fades into the background. You’re not watching the scoreboard. You’re listening for the next laugh.

trust_misplaced.text: She logged off, but the game doesn’t feel fun anymore. You stare at your screen, wondering if you ruined something delicate too soon.

choices.text: Keep it up and do nothing
Message her to apologize
Let her be. If she wants to come back, she will.

unlocked_ending.text: You close the game. No message. You let the silence stretch. Her name fades on your friends list—not removed, just buried. One night, long after, you see her online. You hover over the 'message' button. And you don’t click it. Some people walk into your life like whispers. And leave like ghosts.

resume_connection.text: You type: 'Hey… I’m sorry if I pushed you too much.' You wait. She’s online. The 'typing…' bubble vanishes. Finally: 'It’s okay.' Polite. Distant. Later, you check your friends list. Her name isn’t there anymore.

reunion_goodbye.text: You close Discord. No message. Days pass. Then one night, her name pops up in the lobby: 'Wanna queue again?' You smile. Maybe goodbye wasn’t forever.

silent_stay.text: You don’t push. You just… stay. You play. You listen. At the end of the match, she types: 'I’m sorry I didn’t talk, but I liked your voice.' You reply: 'Your voice is <3<3'—even when she didn’t speak at all.

choices.text: Invite a friend next time to help her feel confident
Encourage her to feel comfortable

friend_established.text: You invite a friend, hoping it helps her feel at ease. She says she’s not ready yet but appreciates your thoughtfulness. You realize… you made her feel safe. And that safety could be the start of something sweet.

encouragement.text: You say: 'No pressure ever to talk. But I liked having you there.' Over time, she begins to say little things. A laugh. A 'Hi.' You don’t rush her. You just stay. And that’s what builds trust—slow, steady warmth.

voice_found.text: She’s still nervous, afraid you might leave because of her English and her struggle to be fluent. She’s hard on herself, always expecting perfection, but you keep reassuring her mistakes are how she’ll learn. For you, that effort means everything. Slowly, she starts sending you voice messages every night, talking about her day. You love it, because it means she’s thinking of you before she sleeps. And that’s a feeling you can’t help but treasure.

choices.text: Confess she has a sexy businesswoman voice
Ask her to read something for you anything just to hear her voice longer

sexy_voice.text: That night, after listening to her latest audio, you can’t help yourself. You say, 'You know… If I’m honest… you’ve got this sexy businesswoman voice. The kind that could close a deal or break a heart in one sentence.' Her reply comes with a soft laugh, the kind that makes your chest warm. 'Stop… you’re making me blush.' But the next night, her audio is longer, smoother, like she’s aware now of what her voice does to you and you realize her voice has quietly become your favorite addiction that you will not leave so easily.

read_for_me.text: You’re obsessed with her voice now, not just with her gameplay, her laugh, her face, but the way every word she speaks wraps around you. You want more. So you ask her to read The Raven, a poem by Edgar Allan Poe, for you, just so you can hear her voice again. She accepts, but with one condition: you have to read to her too, so she can hear your voice in return. It feels like something that was always meant to happen, a quiet exchange of words and hearts. You’re hopeful for what’s next… and already craving it

direct_approach.text: She tilts her head, a little confused but then recognition sparks in her eyes. 'Ohhh… it’s you.' You laugh, the tension melting away. She gestures to the empty seat beside her. The conversation starts with SMITE but soon becomes something more. Hours pass. When you stand to leave, you both hesitate. That quiet, unspoken question hangs between you: When will we see each other again?

subtle_move.text: Her eyes soften in instant recognition. Without hesitation, she crosses the space between you and sits down. 'Guess fate’s got good matchmaking after all.' The conversation flows—unforced, like you’ve been saving words for this day. She admits she stayed up thinking about that one match because it reminded her of you. Time stops mattering. All you notice is her smile, her voice, the way she leans in. Somewhere deep down, you realize: this might be the moment everything changes.

mx_ga.text: The first flight after months of talking about it she’s finally coming to you. Both of you had been counting the days, and now it’s real. You’re nervous, your hands can’t keep still, but the moment you see her walking down the path from the arrival gate, everything else disappears. “Hi, baby,” you say, your voice soft but full of everything you’ve felt these past months. She looks incredible, even more than you’d imagined and in her eyes, there’s a spark that sets something alight inside you. You want to freeze this moment, live in it forever.  “Hi, baby,” she replies, smiling in that way that makes your chest ache. You can tell she’s wishing you’d just kiss her already. And in that instant, you know this isn’t just the end of a wait. It’s the beginning of everything you’ve been hoping for and never imagined it would happen

ga_mx.text: It’s your first time flying alone. Airports aren’t your thing—too many people, too much noise—but none of that matters. You’re coming to see *her*. You’d renewed your passport, dug up your birth certificate, endured endless lines. Now, standing in the terminal with your heart pounding, you know it’s worth it. Because at the end of this trip… she’ll be there.

drunk_truths.text: You start opening up about things you’ve never told anyone before, your voice steady but heart racing. She listens, really listens. When she speaks, it’s with a warmth that seeps through the distance. By the call’s end, you’ve crossed into a different kind of connection—one built on trust that can’t be taken back. You’ve found your person. Your home.

the_promise.text: Without thinking, you say: 'One day, I’ll be there when this happens. No screens. No calls. Just me, making sure you’re okay.' She goes quiet, then whispers: 'I’d like that.' It’s simple, but in that moment, it feels like a promise you’re determined to keep. The miles will disappear. Because it’s her who you want.

send_pic.text: You snap a quick, natural photo and send it. 'Fair’s fair.' Her reply is instant: 'Cute.' That one word lands like a thunderbolt. She adds: 'We make a good-looking team.' You both know she’s not just talking about SMITE anymore.

hot_pic.text: You send a daring picture—a smirk, a flattering angle. Her reply: '…Okay, wow. Didn’t know we were playing like *that*.' The rest of the match is a blur. Neither of you is paying attention anymore. Later that night, your phone buzzes. No words, just a picture. Hotter than yours. A perfect checkmate. The game between you isn’t about kills anymore—it’s about pulling each other closer, one risk at a time.

double_down.text: You don’t back away. 'If we’re going to flirt, I’m going to win that too.' She snorts. 'Oh yeah? Big words.' The match becomes less about victory and more about out-charming each other. By the end, neither remembers the score. All you remember is her laugh lingering in your ears, and the urge to text her again.

soft.text: You surprise her: 'Honestly, I just like talking to you. Game or no game.' She goes quiet. Then: 'Same. That’s… really nice to hear.' The night turns quieter, softer. No teasing, just two voices sharing space in the quiet hum of your headsets. Waiting till it repeats again.
